solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vivacity initially held back mischief-maker

indicators.note: the letter standing first is held back until the end, so the opening E moves to the tail

parts.note: esprit = liveliness, vivacity, a word borrowed from French

explanation.surface: Someone's early high spirits were kept in check, and they turned into a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vivacity initially' tempts you to take a V; 'initially' instead points at the letter to be shunted to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the elves and imps of folklore are the classic mischief-makers.

clue.text: Announcer's maximum annoyance

indicators.note: what an announcer gives us is speech, so we take the sound of the word

parts.note: the top, the highest point, spoken aloud

explanation.surface: A broadcaster at the height of irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: PEAK and PIQUE are said the same; the possessive 'Announcer's' asks for the word as heard, not as spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means resentment at a slight, a flash of wounded pride.

clue.text: Press impatient with a current political barrier

explanation.surface: An impatient newspaper press running with the political current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts you toward I, the physics symbol, but here it is IN, as in the current fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill's name for the Cold War frontier sealing Soviet-bloc Europe off from the West.

clue.text: Agreed to don rotten cheat's pirate garb?

indicators.note: a garment someone dons goes round them
something rotten has broken down

parts.note: anagram fodder; the 's is the surface's possessive

explanation.surface: A pirate costume that agrees with the idea of a dishonest cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: this is only one item of pirate costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the patch over one eye is the stock piece of a stage pirate's dress.

clue.text: Artist's medium discomfort after short illness

indicators.note: a short word is one cut down, so GOUT loses its last letter

parts.note: gout, with its final T cut

explanation.surface: An ailing artist feels unwell after a brief illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like it describes the discomfort (a middling amount) but belongs with 'Artist's' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this opaque watercolour paint is one of the media a painter works in.

clue.text: President with the heart for angry demagogy

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the five in angry
the ranting speech of a demagogue

explanation.surface: A president with a taste for angry populist speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry demagogy' reads as one phrase, but only 'demagogy' is RANT; 'angry' supplies just its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Ulysses S. Grant, Civil War general, was the 18th holder of the US office.

clue.text: Modernised vans from urban parade went out together

indicators.note: the van is the front of anything, so the vans of these words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
dated = went out as a couple

explanation.surface: Refurbished vans leave a city parade in convoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vans' reads as vehicles in the parade, but a van is the front, as in vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean brought into line with the present day.

clue.text: Appeal in protest, offering help

indicators.note: one thing sits in another

explanation.surface: Someone lodges an appeal against a protest, offering to help.
explanation.walkthrough: SA for sex appeal is a crossword standby; 'Appeal' looks like a legal plea.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: the word describes someone obliging and eager to please, ready to go along and lend a hand.

clue.text: Artist is in Paris, taking in Rodin on vacation

indicators.note: to take in a lodger is to have them inside your house
a word on vacation has emptied out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Rodin with its middle letters gone

explanation.surface: An artist in Paris goes to see Rodin's work while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin, the French sculptor, fits the Paris scene so well that he looks like the answer's neighbour rather than fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Max Ernst was a German-born Dadaist and Surrealist painter.

clue.text: Meandering soldiers put in charge

indicators.note: the soldiers are put inside the word for charge

parts.note: to charge formally with a crime

explanation.surface: Wandering troops have been placed under someone's command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in charge' reads as a single phrase meaning appointed; split it, and 'charge' is INDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a winding route or a rambling answer never goes straight to the point.

clue.text: Pen triter works to read

indicators.note: the letters are worked, kneaded into a new shape

explanation.surface: A writer produces rather hackneyed works for people to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun for the writer's output; it is the verb that jumbles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of making out meaning, as when you read a situation or a dream.

clue.text: Dog's head drops down

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dog droops its head in dejection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops down' looks like one phrase for the dog's head; the definition is 'down', as in downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to down a glass is to empty it in one go.

clue.text: Increase housing bill, inspiring fear

parts.note: a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: A steep rise in a housing bill is enough to frighten anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing bill' reads as rent or mortgage; 'housing' is the container and 'bill' is TAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means formidable, commanding fear or awed respect.

clue.text: Recalled old party host holding English stringed instrument

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: MC = master of ceremonies, a host

explanation.surface: Someone remembers an old party host who kept an English harpsichord.
explanation.walkthrough: Put E inside MC, then read the whole string backwards. 'Recalled' looks like memory, but it means called back.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Italian word for the harpsichord, whose strings are plucked from a keyboard.

clue.text: It's evident prison transmuted a modern criminal

indicators.note: criminal letters have gone wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clearly, a spell in jail changed an up-to-date criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transmuted' looks like the anagram indicator but is part of the fodder; 'criminal' does the shuffling. Quod is British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose paraphrase: the Latin tag 'which was to be demonstrated' closes a proof, declaring the point now plain.

clue.text: Chinese finally sought after car dealer

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of sought

explanation.surface: A Chinese buyer at last tracks down a car dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car dealer' looks like the definition as a unit, but the car is wordplay and only 'dealer' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trader who buys and sells goods.

clue.text: Satellite rattles when blown about

indicators.note: letters blown about by the wind land in a new order

explanation.surface: A satellite shakes and rattles when buffeted.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram hides in plain sight: 'rattles' looks like the satellite's own noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the 1962 communications craft that first relayed live TV across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Sweet nothing, with husband being ace

parts.note: H = husband; this is the letter that goes
A = ace, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: Sweet nothings from a husband who is simply wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet nothing' reads as a phrase of endearment; split it, and 'Sweet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a chewy confection of sugar or honey, nuts and egg white.

clue.text: Sharp stuff from fault-finder having delayed resistance with drug

indicators.note: the R (resistance) is held back

explanation.surface: A critic's sharp words, fuelled by a drug and put off for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: R = resistance, as in physics. Push the R of CRITIC two places later and it becomes CITRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the compound that gives lemons and limes their sharp, sour taste.

clue.text: A shy person, traveller stops during races

parts.note: the TT races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A timid traveller halts while the races are on.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle race series held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone turned inward, reserved and uneasy in company.

clue.text: Fish caught by one in paper, wriggling

indicators.note: the one is placed in the paper, as fish is wrapped in it
the letters of PAPER wriggle into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish caught by an angler is wrapped in newspaper, still wriggling.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards; wriggle PAPER to RAPPE and slip the I in.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a North American freshwater sunfish.

clue.text: Tense one working and failing

parts.note: a past tense for ongoing action

explanation.surface: A stressed worker who is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the worker; it is the grammatical tense. 'Failing' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: a failing is a flaw or weakness of character.

clue.text: Animal in parable, or in another form

indicators.note: the letters are put into another form, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An animal appears in a parable, or perhaps in some other story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parable, or' supplies all nine letters, the comma ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the great white bear of the Arctic.

clue.text: Recruiter in French car

explanation.surface: A recruiting officer driving a French car.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce. 'In' looks like the recruiter sitting in the car, but 'in French' is EN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one who signs people up, as for a course or an army.

clue.text: Evens out site of a portico

indicators.note: throwing out the even-placed letters keeps only the odd ones

parts.note: keep the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters, ignoring the spaces

explanation.surface: Levelling the ground where a colonnade will stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evens out' reads as levelling; here it discards letters 2, 4 and 6.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Greek architecture: a covered colonnade or porch.

clue.text: River bird one's seen on a ship

explanation.surface: A river bird is spotted aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taff is a river in South Wales; the rail is a wading bird. The definition is a vague pointer that only makes sense once solved.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: this is the rail round the stern of a ship, so one of the things seen aboard.

clue.text: Female to get around breezy, fantastic place

parts.note: to land a job = to get it

explanation.surface: A woman goes travelling around a breezy, marvellous spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get around' looks like travelling; split them, and 'to get' is a word for secure while 'around' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an enchanted realm of fantasy, the home of the little people.

clue.text: Sacked on Thursday, was very sore?

indicators.note: in an across clue A on B puts A after B, so the sacking word comes second

parts.note: the usual short form of the day
to sack a town = to plunder it

explanation.surface: Fired on a Thursday, someone was understandably upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' looks like fired from a job; it is plundered, as a city is sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a wound that pulsed with pain was very sore.

clue.text: Old wine unruly adolescent brought up

parts.note: a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth tearaway

explanation.surface: A badly behaved teenager was raised on old wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress, a byword for delinquency. 'Brought up' looks like upbringing; it is digging up.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: what archaeologists dig out has been brought up from the ground.

clue.text: Covering king and a couple of leaders

parts.note: two leaders: ER, the Queen, and a chief

explanation.surface: A king and two chiefs share one covering.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; 'a couple of leaders' asks for two separate words for a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a square of cloth tied over the head is a covering.

clue.text: Totter up with beer, welcoming old musical style

explanation.surface: Someone staggers to their feet with a beer and an old tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totter' looks like stagger; read it as tot-ter, someone who tots up, so a COUNTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the art of weaving independent melodic lines together, as in Bach.

clue.text: School subject one grasped by quiet determination

explanation.surface: A school subject taught by quiet determination.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a British school subject; SCIENCE is the tempting wrong subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: toughness, the capacity to keep going and bounce back.

clue.text: Boss has drink, on second

explanation.surface: The boss has a drink and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On second' reads as a second round; both words are short forms, the memo's 'concerning' and 'just a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the person in overall charge.

clue.text: Man stops erring by a crude vice

indicators.note: the letters err, straying from their order

explanation.surface: A man gives up his wayward life of crude vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By a crude' is the fodder; the surface makes 'crude vice' look like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: indulgence in sensual excess, vice in bulk.

clue.text: According to girl I don't know, this is a sprinkler

parts.note: a girl's name, short for Gillian

explanation.surface: A girl admits she has no idea what this sprinkler is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a shrug of ignorance at an obscure word, which the wordplay then spells out.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the brush or perforated globe a priest uses to sprinkle holy water.

clue.text: Riding train, the setter's giving nothing away

explanation.surface: The setter rides a train, keeping a poker face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is 'the setter has', I'VE, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a blank face that shows no feeling gives nothing away.

clue.text: Lively home by Spanish city esteemed highly

explanation.surface: A lively home in a much admired Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain; 'esteemed highly' together make one word, not two.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: filled with energy, so lively.

clue.text: Visitor for Christmas day, one around US resort

parts.note: the man who calls at Christmas

explanation.surface: A Christmas visitor stops in at an American holiday resort for a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container indicator; it is CA, short for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a Californian beach city on the edge of Los Angeles.

clue.text: Bit by bit, returned animals with good sense

indicators.note: returned things go back the way they came

explanation.surface: Animals are gradually brought back by someone sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned animals' looks like pets brought home; it is the word written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: proceeding one stage at a time.

clue.text: Passing border in record time, heading for Laos

indicators.note: the border is placed in the middle of record-plus-time
the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Crossing the frontier in record time on the road to Laos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing border' looks like a travel phrase; 'Passing' is the definition, and 'in record time' is literal wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective synonym: short-lived, soon over, passing.

clue.text: Referred to broadcast, ignoring one's daughter

indicators.note: ignoring one's leaves out the letters IS

explanation.surface: Something mentioned on air leaves out one person's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is I'S, one is: take IS out of ADVERTISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal verb synonym: to advert to a topic is to mention it.

clue.text: Ball and function from the right country club

indicators.note: read from the right means read backwards

explanation.surface: A ball and a function held at a country club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball and function' look like social events; they are a round letter and a maths function.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty cryptic description: the North Atlantic alliance is a club whose members are countries.

clue.text: Trust man to train pets

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leave it to a man to train the family pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pets' looks like animals; it means sulks, as in 'in a pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated sense: a pet is a fit of peevish temper, a childish outburst.

clue.text: For high tea, do supply alcohol

indicators.note: read as supple-y, the letters bend into a new shape

explanation.surface: An instruction to serve drinks at a high tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like provide; read it as the adverb of supple.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the idiom names a drink taken to cure a hangover.

clue.text: Mean, say, to be getting on

explanation.surface: Being stingy, you might say, comes with getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like miserly; it is the arithmetic mean.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical synonym: sum the values and divide by how many there are.

clue.text: Fake news to support a leaderless country

indicators.note: a leaderless word has lost its first letter

explanation.surface: Disinformation used to prop up a country with no leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaderless country is an African state that has lost its U.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: slanted or false information spread to sway opinion.

clue.text: Technique for selling new design

explanation.surface: A sales method for marketing a new product design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New design' reads as one phrase; 'new' is N and 'design' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a repeated decorative motif, as on wallpaper.

clue.text: He won't accept obsolete coin

definitions.meaning: one who refuses to admit something
a small French coin long out of use

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are said differently: one rhymes with 'flier', the old coin sounds like 'den-ee-ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who denies refuses to accept; the old French penny was a coin of small value.

clue.text: Flier's welcome in armed service

indicators.note: the welcome is enlisted in the service, placed inside it

explanation.surface: An airman is welcomed into the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a pilot, which suits the armed-service surface; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the large black crow is a bird, so something that flies.

clue.text: Live in perfect tower

indicators.note: to live in a place is to be inside it, so the word for live goes inside the word for perfect

parts.note: a form of the verb to be, which means to live

explanation.surface: Living in an ideal tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' is ARE, a form of the verb to be; MINT for perfect comes from 'in mint condition'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the slender tower beside a mosque from which the call to prayer is given.

clue.text: US cities hosting a creature from Africa

indicators.note: the two cities host A between them

explanation.surface: American cities hosting an African animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The two standard city abbreviations sit either side of the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: On the point of retiring, cut expenditure

indicators.note: the plural word is cut short, losing its final S

parts.note: money going out, usually plural, with its final S cut

explanation.surface: A retiring official is ordered to cut spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut expenditure' looks like a budget order; the expenditure word is OUTGOINGS, and 'cut' docks its S.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective synonym: an official about to leave office is on the way out.

clue.text: Missile launch site shelters right in the shade

parts.note: the line darts players throw from

explanation.surface: A missile launch site keeps the right hidden in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands in British pubs; the missiles are darts, not rockets.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a yellowish-brown earth colour, one shade among many.

clue.text: Almost time for parting word

parts.note: old word for near, so almost

explanation.surface: It is nearly time to say goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost time' reads as one phrase, but each word supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: said on parting in the evening, short for good night.

clue.text: Very effusive towards semiotician, with hard journey nearly done

parts.note: to be all over someone = to fuss over them
Roland Barthes, French theorist of signs

explanation.surface: A fan gushes over a French thinker after a hard trip is almost complete.
explanation.walkthrough: Roland Barthes wrote on semiotics, the study of signs.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the result is settled and only the celebrating or complaining remains.

clue.text: French novel all told briefly after the beginning

indicators.note: told briefly, IN ALL is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the germ of an idea is its beginning
in all = all told, with the final L cut

explanation.surface: A French novel, summed up briefly after its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After the beginning' reads as 'past the opening pages'; here 'after' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Émile Zola's 1885 novel of a coal miners' strike.

clue.text: Article by poet is going slowly

explanation.surface: An essay by a poet is making slow progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is going slowly' reads as a remark about the poet; the definition is the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term: the Italian direction for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Revealing hypocrisy in empty society

indicators.note: the hypocrisy is found in the society, placed inside its shell
an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: society emptied leaves its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Exposing the hypocrisy of a hollow society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revealing' looks like exposing a truth; it describes skimpy clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: skimpy clothing that covers little is revealing.
